ordered_diagnoses: Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum

s1.syndrome_frame: Altered mental status with catatonia and autonomic dysfunction
salient_findings: Disturbed consciousness with Glasgow scale score of 7
Rigidity, negativism, mutism, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, and stupor
Elevated creatine phosphokinase and liver enzymes
key_facts: 44-year-old man with a history of schizophrenia
Under antipsychotic treatment with risperidone and antiparkinsonian drug Biperiden
Rigidity, negativism, mutism, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, and stupor
Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score of 25/69
Unremarkable chest X-ray and cerebral CT
Brain MRI showing round lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum with restricted diffusion

shortlist: Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum

shortlist.label: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is under antipsychotic treatment with risperidone and presents with fever, rigidity, and elevated creatine phosphokinase

shortlist.label: Malignant Catatonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score and exhibits catatonic symptoms such as mutism, catalepsy, and waxy flexibility

shortlist.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and a round lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum on brain MRI

shortlist.label: Serotonin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is under antipsychotic treatment with risperidone, which can increase serotonin levels, and presents with fever, rigidity, and autonomic dysfunction

shortlist.label: Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a round lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum on brain MRI with restricted diffusion, suggesting cytotoxic edema

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including rigidity, negativism, mutism, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, and stupor, along with a high Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale score of 25/69, are characteristic of catatonia. The presence of fever, tachycardia, and elevated CPK and liver enzymes further supports the diagnosis of malignant catatonia, which is a life-threatening condition that can occur in patients with catatonia.

rejected.label: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient is on antipsychotic treatment, the absence of treatment withdrawal and the presence of catatonic symptoms suggest malignant catatonia over neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

rejected.label: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms such as seizures, memory loss, or changes in behavior that are typical of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, and the brain MRI findings do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Serotonin Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms do not include the classic triad of serotonin syndrome (altered mental status, neuromuscular abnormalities, and autonomic dysfunction), and the use of risperidone and Biperiden does not typically cause serotonin syndrome.

rejected.label: Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum
rejected.why: While the brain MRI shows a lesion in the splenium of the corpus callosum, the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings are more consistent with malignant catatonia than a primary lesion of the corpus callosum.
